rows.notes: The study is a literature review (title 'Big Data in Smart Farming <U+2013> A review'; Section 2 describes a systematic literature survey of Web of Science, Scopus and grey literature). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or model runs. Its discussion of data ownership, privacy, power concentration and governance (Sections 4.4.1, 4.5, 5) is a synthesis of cited literature, not a primary result on remote sensing and uptake or concentration among larger producers.

Same study: a literature review with no own primary data. Statements that data-ownership, privacy and security issues can inhibit developments and that data may concentrate in the hands of big players are drawn from cited sources (e.g. Lesser, 2014; Gilpin, 2015b), not from the authors' own evidence; no evidence specific to app-based scheduling.

notes: Document is a complete review article (Wolfert et al., 2017, Agricultural Systems 153:69-80). It develops a conceptual framework and synthesises peer-reviewed and grey literature; the authors themselves note that a reliable quantitative analysis was not possible. No primary research reported, so Q1 is 'no' for both rows.
